honesty_notes: abstract is a SHORT PARAPHRASE of the guide's description, NOT the official abstract. Replace with the official abstract from the schedule page on Monday if you demo it as such.
start_time is null where no guide gave a time — do not present those as scheduled. Conflict detection in seed-and-search.py only runs on talks with known times.
speakers is [] unless a guide named one (Neel Shah; Soham Ghadge). No speaker names were invented.
This is a demo seed (26 talks), not the full programme — the full schedule has hundreds of sessions.
provenance: Official schedule page, events.linuxfoundation.org/kubecon-cloudnativecon-north-america/program/schedule/ — checked 2026-11-08; it renders a time grid only, no session titles in the text fetch, so titles/times below come from the guides, not a scrape of it. Room/day for the Monday co-located events was confirmed there (Cloud Native AI + Inference Day, Room 254; Agentics Day, Grand Ballroom ACE; Platform Engineering Day, Grand Ballroom BDF; BackstageCon, Room 255 EF; ArgoCon, Room 151).

Matthew Wong, 'KubeCon North America 2026 Guide: AI Track, Co-located Days' — https://www.matthewswong.com/en/blog/kubecon-na-2026-salt-lake-city-guide/ — Monday 10:40/11:15/11:50 sessions, Tuesday 11:30 sessions, keynote times. Read 2026-10-17 by that author; times are a snapshot and can change.

StackGen, 'KubeCon NA 2026: The Production Stories Worth Hearing' — https://stackgen.com/blog/kubecon-na-2026-production-stories-worth-hearing — AI/SRE/platform talk titles, BackstageCon times, Neel Shah ArgoCon lightning talk.

Broadcom/VMware, 'AI, Kubernetes, and Cloud Native Innovations: Broadcom at KubeCon North America 2026' — https://blogs.vmware.com/cloud-foundation/2026/10/12/ai-kubernetes-and-cloud-native-innovations-broadcom-at-kubecon-north-america-2026/ — Monday 10:10 keynote in Room 254; Tuesday 17:30 TAG panel; F5 session times via VMblog Q&A — https://vmblog.com/qa/f5-at-kubecon-cloudnativecon-na-2026-securing-ai-inference-and-agentic-traffic-in-kubernetes/

talks.abstract: Keynote on making AI delivery resilient in production, where the hard part is operating the system, not the model.

talks.abstract: Observing llm-d inference at scale on Kubernetes — what to measure when serving models in production.

talks.abstract: Building GPU-aware observability for inference with Fluent Bit and OpenTelemetry telemetry pipelines.

talks.abstract: Platform patterns for keeping agent state durable and recoverable instead of losing it between steps.

talks.abstract: Reactive agents over MCP using continuous queries instead of polling for changes.

talks.abstract: Guardrails for agents and sandboxes doing GitOps with Flux.

talks.abstract: Panel on cloud native infrastructure in the AI era — what changes when clusters serve models and agents.
